questions.question: Why is a 'How to Test' section essential in PR descriptions?
choices: It's required by GitHub's PR template
It tells reviewers exactly how to verify the changes work correctly
It automatically runs the tests for you
questions.explanation: Without testing instructions, reviewers must guess how to verify changes. This slows down review and increases the chance of shipping untested code.

questions.question: When should you include a breaking change notice in a PR description?
choices: Only when the PR touches more than 5 files
When the changes may require code modifications in dependent projects or consumers
Every time the PR is larger than 100 lines
Only for PRs that modify package.json
questions.explanation: Breaking changes affect downstream consumers. Flagging them ensures teams that depend on your code know they need to update their code when they pull the changes.

questions.question: What makes a good changes list in a PR description?
choices: Specific bullet points that describe what changed and why
A link to the diff without any explanation
questions.explanation: Specific bullet points let reviewers quickly understand the scope of changes without reading every line of code. Each point should be clear and actionable.
